Cash flow {col:ra.cash_flow} a year on {col:ra.cash_in} put in: cash-on-cash return {col:ra.coc}. DSCR (NOI divided by loan payments) {col:ra.dscr}. Checks: {col:ra.coc_flag}, {col:ra.dscr_flag}. Check with your own adviser before you rely on these figures.
Flip profit forecast {col:fa.flip_id} of {set:company}, dated {today}, for {col:fa.address}.
Purchase {col:fa.purchase} with closing costs {col:fa.buy_closing}, rehab {col:fa.rehab}, ARV {col:fa.arv}, {col:fa.months_to_sell} months to sell at {col:fa.holding_monthly} holding cost a month.
Selling costs {col:fa.selling_costs}. Holding costs {col:fa.holding}. Profit forecast {col:fa.profit}, a return of {col:fa.roi} on the cost.
The 70% rule (offer at most 70% of the ARV minus the rehab) gives a highest offer of {col:fa.max_offer}. Rule check: {col:fa.rule_flag}. Check with your own adviser about tax on a gain.
Offer letter to the seller agent
We offer {col:offers.offer_price} for the property at {col:offers.address} (asking price {col:offers.asking_price}).

This offer stays open until {col:offers.valid_until}. It depends on a satisfactory inspection, a satisfactory due diligence check and the loan being approved. Status of the offer: {col:offers.status}.
Please send your answer to the closing coordinator and to us. Check your own local rules on how an offer must be written and delivered.
Due diligence request for one item
Property: {col:dd.address} (deal {col:dd.deal_id}). Item: {col:dd.item}. Owner of the item: {col:dd.owner}.
Due on {col:dd.due_date}. Done on {col:dd.done_on}. Status: {col:dd.status}. Timing: {col:dd.timing}, days late {col:dd.days_late}.
Please send the document or the answer by the due date. Check your own local rules on the checks needed before a purchase.
Inspection repair request to the seller
Property: {col:insp.address}. Inspected on {col:insp.date} by {col:insp.inspector}. Issues found: {col:insp.issues_found}.
Our repair estimate is {col:insp.repair_estimate}, which is {col:insp.cost_share} of the offer price of {col:insp.price}. Repair flag: {col:insp.flag}.
We ask the seller to repair the issues, to give a credit for them or to lower the price. Please answer before the offer expires. Check your own local rules on repairs and disclosures.
Lender package cover sheet for quote {col:quotes.quote_id} of {set:company}, dated {today}.

Purchase price {col:quotes.price}. Loan asked {col:quotes.loan_amount} ({col:quotes.ltv} of the price) over {col:quotes.term_years} years. Quoted rate {col:quotes.rate} with {col:quotes.points} points. Monthly payment {col:quotes.payment}. Cash to close {col:quotes.cash_to_close}.

Enclosed: the purchase contract, the rental analysis, proof of funds, the rent roll (the list of units, tenants and rents) and the inspection summary. Check your own local rules on what a lender must receive.
Weekly pipeline report for one stage

Open Start and type your company name and your own targets in the yellow cells: the cash-on-cash return you want, the lowest DSCR, the loan share, the 70% rule, the management fee and the closing share.

Write every deal you look at on Deals with the asking price, your offer, the rehab budget, the ARV and the rent. The offer share of asking, the total cost, the gross yield, the cash needed and the decision flag fill in.

Run the Rental analyser or the Flip analyser before you offer, then save the figures on Rental analyses or Flip analyses. NOI, cap rate, cash flow, cash-on-cash and DSCR fill in and show if the deal meets your targets.
Use Maximum rental offer and Maximum flip offer to find the highest price that still works, and the Offer ladder to plan three offers.
Record each offer on Offers with the counter-offer and the accepted price. The gap to asking and the offer flag show which offers expire soon.
Check the value and the rent on Sales comparables, Rental comparables and Market rent by town, or use the Value estimator and the Rent estimator with three comparables.
Write the work on Rehab estimates by category with a contingency, or get a quick budget from Rehab quick budget.
Track every check on Due diligence and every call on Follow-ups. Items left open past their date are marked overdue.
Record each inspection on Inspections and each lender quote on Loan quotes. The repair share of the price and the cash to close fill in.
Read Deal sources, Pass reasons and Pipeline stages every week to see where the deals that close come from and why you pass on the rest.

Use the 14 calculators: rental and flip analysers, two maximum offers, closing costs, loan payment, rent and value estimators, rehab budget, five-year IRR, break-even, offer ladder, a what-if grid and a scorecard.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text already written (28 messages).
Read the Deal Pipeline Dashboard and Charts every week: deals by month, status, source and town, offer acceptance, cap rate, cash-on-cash, DSCR, rehab, inspections, loan rates and due diligence.

Every loan with payment, balance and balloon date
One row for each loan; payment, balance today, share paid down, months to the balloon (the day the remaining balance is due) and 12-month interest fill in.
Every loan payment with interest, principal and balance
One row for each monthly payment with the interest, the principal and the balance after it; the due date and the days paid late fill in, so a late payment stands out.
The 16 properties with the price and the value now; the gain against the price fills in, so each loan is read against what the property is worth.
Valuations of each property over time
One row for each value estimate (agent opinion, appraisal or comparable sales); the share of the value now fills in, so you see how the value moved before a refinance.
Loan-to-value and equity for each property
One row for each property; the loan balance, value, loan-to-value (loan divided by value), equity and room to borrow fill in, with a flag above your level.
One row for each held property; rent, costs, NOI (rent minus operating costs, before loan payments), loan payments, DSCR (NOI divided by loan payments) and cushion fill in.
Refinance options with the saving and the break-even
One row for each refinance offer; the new loan, the new payment, the saving a month and the months to break even (the costs divided by the monthly saving) fill in, so you see which offers pay back.
Lenders and what each one offers
One row for each product a lender offers with the highest loan share, the lowest rate and the way to reach them; the loans and the balance you carry with that lender fill in.
Rate resets and rate offers for each loan
One row for each rate reset or rate offer with the old and the new rate; the change, its effect on the payment each month and a direction flag fill in.
Effect on the payment each month
Balloon dates with the plan for each
One row for each way to settle a balloon loan (refinance, sell, pay from cash or ask for an extension) with its status; the balance due, the days left and the flag fill in.
Payoff quotes with the date they stay valid
One row for each payoff quote from a lender with the amount and the valid-until date; the balance today, the days left and a validity flag fill in.
Loan covenant checks with a pass or fail
One row for each test a lender sets (DSCR, loan-to-value, cash reserve) with the level required and the level reached; the pass or fail fills in.
Interest-only periods with rate and monthly interest
One row for each interest-only period of a loan with its rate; the balance, the interest each month and the months left fill in.
Private lender terms and their true yearly cost
One row for each private lender offer or loan with points (a fee as a percent of the loan), rate, months and fee; the true yearly rate fills in.
Line of credit draws and repayments
One row for each draw on the line of credit or each repayment (a repayment is a negative amount); the balance after it, the room left and the share used fill in.
Documents each lender asks for, with due dates
One row for each document a lender needs with the due date and the date it was received; the timing flag and the days late fill in, so a missing document stands out.
Rent roll: the list of units, tenants and rents
One row for each rental unit with the market rent and the rent charged; the rent below the market rent (loss to lease) fills in.
One row for each unit and month with the rent due and the amount paid; the DSCR page adds up what was collected in 12 months.
Operating costs by property and year
One row for each property and year with the operating costs (tax, insurance, fee, repairs, utilities) and the months covered; the cost a month fills in and feeds the DSCR page.
